headline: JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon said the bank will not let unvetted outside AI agents into its systems because of the risk of rogue agents.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the remark came on the earnings call of Tuesday 13 October, before the window; it describes a bank policy already in force for retail customers.
importance_line: Customers of the bank and the apps that connect to it are affected first, since the bank is deciding who carries the loss if an AI agent misbehaves, but the bank gave no timeline for letting agents do more.
summary: PYMNTS reports that on JPMorgan Chase's third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 October, Jamie Dimon, chief executive of the biggest US bank, said "You don't want rogue agents, and there could be thousands of them," and that people who use outside agents should understand "the liability transfer." The block already applies to retail customers: outside agents cannot act for a customer or log in with their credentials, and can see balances read-only through connectors such as Plaid when the customer allows it, a JPMorgan spokeswoman told CNBC.
